q1: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2: SELECT A.CUSTOMER_ID AS CUSTOMER_ID FROM (SELECT CUSTOMER_ID, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT(PRODUCT_KEY) ORDER BY PRODUCT_KEY) AS NEW FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID) A WHERE NEW = (SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT(PRODUCT_KEY) ORDER BY PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT A.CUSTOMER_ID AS CUSTOMER_ID FROM (SELECT CUSTOMER_ID, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT(PRODUCT_KEY) ORDER BY PRODUCT_KEY) AS NEW FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID) A WHERE NEW = (SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT(PRODUCT_KEY) ORDER BY PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
counterexample: INSERT INTO PRODUCT (PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1), (2), (3); INSERT INTO CUSTOMER (CUSTOMER_ID, PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1, 1), (1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 1), (2, 2);
explanation: Q1 checks if the number of distinct products purchased by a customer is equal to the total number of distinct products in the database. Q2 checks if the sorted, concatenated list of distinct products purchased by a customer matches the sorted, concatenated list of all distinct products in the database.
counterexample_dsp: A customer who has purchased all products in the database, and another customer who has purchased all products except for one.
